\caption{Comparison of \must{} and \tool{} under timing regimes taken from real systems (all times in ms, one tick = 1\,ms; YARN in 1\,s ticks). Networks: [A] same-region cross-AZ $U{=}1$ (Azure AZ round trip below about 2\,ms), [B] continental $U{=}65$ (etcd tuning guide, 130\,ms round trip), [C] intercontinental $U{=}200$ (etcd, 350 to 400\,ms), [D] degraded $U{=}2\,500$ (etcd election cap), [E] partition-delayed $U{=}90\,000$ (GitHub 2012); suffix p: $L$ is half the median. Times are seconds on one core, medians of three runs unless marked $^\dagger$ (fewer runs) or $^{\ddagger n}$ (run with $n$ workers; wall time not comparable); $>t$: not finished after $t$ seconds. \emph{Exec.} counts all complete execution graphs including blocked ones and those with a failed assertion; \emph{Viol.} counts the graphs with at least one failed assertion, once per graph. Configuration columns: lease: clients, rounds, TTL, client pause ($b$ is the boundary $\mathit{TTL}-2(U-L)-\sd$); SWIM: probe period and suspicion timeout; BRP: $L{=}0.5$ is the half-unit grid of the transit interval $(0,T_D]$; YARN: ticks of the 1\,s NM heartbeat.}\label{tab:evaluation-full}\\
